# Codex Pet Dock 0.3.0 Beta

**Windows 11 64-bit only.**

Codex Pet Dock puts the information people check most often directly under
the existing Codex desktop pet:

- **WEEK LEFT** - remaining weekly quota reported by Codex;
- **WEEK TOKENS** - local weekly Token activity estimated from local Codex
  session logs;
- click the base for a bilingual detail card with reset time, cache ratio,
  fresh/output Tokens, sessions, and data freshness.

It does not create a second floating widget and does not modify the Codex
installation, `app.asar`, pet assets, or source code.

## Install

Download **`CodexPetDock-Setup-0.3.0-beta.exe`**, double-click it, and follow
the installer. The installer is per-user, needs no administrator permission,
preserves settings during upgrades, and can be removed from Windows Settings
> Apps > Installed apps.

The ZIP is for portable/developer use. Do not download GitHub's automatically
generated **Source code** archives if you want the Windows installer.

## Included

- nine built-in DPI-aware base themes;
- English by default, with instant Simplified Chinese switching;
- safe data-only custom themes and Codex-assisted theme creation;
- adaptive following, pet switching, hiding, restart and anchor recovery;
- launch-at-sign-in, single-instance protection, update check, clean upgrade
  and uninstall;
- native C# quota probe; end users do not need Node.js, npm or a .NET SDK;
- 5-minute normal refresh, immediate retry when Windows network connectivity
  returns, and bounded 15-300 second backoff after service failures;
- no quota probing while no pet is visible;
- privacy-preserving local Token index using hashed file identifiers and
  numeric aggregates only.

## Windows Beta notice

This Beta is not Authenticode-signed yet, so Windows may display
**Unknown publisher**. Download only from this repository and verify the
SHA-256 value in `SHA256SUMS.txt`. You do not need to disable Microsoft
Defender or other security protection.

## Performance snapshot

Measured on Windows 11 / i7-11800H:

- visible-idle CPU: about **0.21% of total 16-thread capacity**;
- visible-idle working set: about **167 MB**;
- quota probe does not remain running while idle;
- native warm-probe peak was about **31% lower** than the previous Node
  reference.
